label: Feet + gait documented together
significance: Bilateral foot pain, abnormal gait, deformity and pressure lesions are already one presenting problem.

label: Neurology question framed as gait + feet + muscle tension
significance: Primary care explicitly sends an integrated gait–feet–tone question toward Neurology.

label: Marked bilateral leg tone joins the foot/gait problem
significance: Pathological tone is documented before specialist admission; the clinical object is still integrated.

label: Neurology finds severe Parkinsonism + dystonic-looking gait + structural feet
significance: The specialist now holds neurological findings and structural foot findings at the same time.

label: Possible secondary peripheral neuropathy; relationship left 'Not clear'
significance: A neurological differential is created but not resolved. The patient-derived separation is strengthened as 'markedly divorced'.

label: Clear plan declared while foot relationship remains unresolved
significance: Plan-level clarity and relationship-level uncertainty coexist in the same portable account.

label: Established Protest before closure
significance: The patient directly challenges the adequacy of the foot disposition. Residual uncertainty becomes known and contested.

label: Protest omitted from portable founding account
significance: The selected branch travels; the fact that the branch was expressly contested does not.

label: Feet routed to Podiatry without identified resolution rule
significance: Routing transfers the local problem, but the record identifies no owner or test for resolving the 'Not clear' neurological relationship.

label: Podiatry localises the problem at the left fifth MTPJ
significance: Podiatry begins acquiring a precise local mechanical/structural truth: recurrent callus at the left fifth metatarsophalangeal region.

label: Procyclidine withdrawal: restless feet + walk falling apart
significance: Neurological treatment-state perturbation changes feet and gait together within months of discharge.

label: Fifth-MTPJ HD enucleated to pin-prick haem; site specifically offloaded
significance: The visible lesion is taken to the safe debridement endpoint and the same site is treated as a loading problem requiring offloading and an insole.

label: Insole fitted; fifth-MTPJ HD again enucleated
significance: The same focal site persists despite prior debridement and targeted mechanical intervention.

label: Fifth-MTPJ callus persists beside clawed toes
significance: The recurrent pressure lesion is documented alongside deforming toe posture.

label: Neurologist records rapid return of outside-left-foot phenomenon off procyclidine
significance: Neurology now holds dynamic treatment-state information affecting the same outside-left-foot territory Podiatry is repeatedly offloading.

label: Persistent left-foot pain; new insoles with fifth-foot cut-out
significance: Podiatry reinforces the mechanical model by again redesigning pressure distribution around the same site.

label: Callus overlying HD still present at left fifth MTPJ
significance: The same structural site remains a durable failure point at the end of the surviving Podiatry series.

label: GP reconnects feet with tone/gait/Parkinson's and marks 'No neuropathy'
significance: Primary care regenerates the original integrated formulation and does not present neuropathy as an established finding.

label: Podiatry pathway ends in surviving record
significance: The local structural pathway ceases. No documented automatic return route reopens the unresolved neurological relationship.

label: Severe foot pain persists despite high-dose pregabalin; Sinemet timing matters
significance: Later evidence crosses the founding boundary, but the painful object is partly recast as 'leg pain and shuffling' when OFF-related dependence is recognised.

label: GP recognises this as the original presentation
significance: The originating clinician recovers the integrated feet–tone–gait object sent into Neurology years earlier.

label: Neurologist says overnight onset is not characteristic of peripheral neuropathy
significance: The neuropathy hypothesis is qualified but not retired; 'Not clear' remains operationally alive.

label: Feet improve when Sinemet acts; CR introduced
significance: The feet are explicitly documented as changing with dopaminergic treatment state.

label: 'If there is a degree of peripheral neuropathy here…'
significance: Eight years after 'perhaps secondary peripheral neuropathy … Not clear', neuropathy remains conditional rather than established or excluded.

label: Historical pathway challenged
significance: The complaint asks why the relationship was not revisited earlier despite accumulating treatment-state evidence.

label: Profound CR relief accepted; historical continuity still invoked
significance: The clinical facts materially move while the founding information state is not globally reconstructed; the historical letters are used as part of the answer.
